title: A source flux bound limits the Gaia20cdd ice-band depth to 0.258 for the stated warm-dust model
abstract: We test whether ice absorption of a separate infrared source can explain the reported 3.1 um band of Gaia20cdd while largely missing the star. An analytic flux bound permits arbitrary stellar dust columns and positive mixtures of thermal sources. With the central published optical and red-infrared fluxes, a clear stellar reference, infrared opacity no larger than optical opacity, source temperatures at or below 650 K, and emissivity indices from 0 to 2, the band depth is at most 0.258. The reported central depth is 0.33. A numerical covering model with a specified ordinary ice law gives about 0.169. The bound allows stellar infrared extinction instead of equating fitted excess with source flux. Combined shifts in uncertain inputs can remove the exclusion. Hot sources, unusual emissivity, persistent stellar extinction and continuum errors remain open. This is a conditional model constraint, not a new ice detection. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and reproduction steps are included.

display.caption: Analytic and numerical upper band-depth limits under the stated source and stellar reference assumptions. The conservative red-bin endpoint limit is 0.258; the curves use 4.7 um.
